title: The Rain in Bluegate Yard
theme: Patient truth matters more than a clean-looking case when the poor are easiest to hang.
style: Write as a soot-dark Victorian London procedural: gaslit 1888 docklands, river fog, wet cobbles, public-house murmurs, and plain-clothes inquiry work, in crisp, observant, morally alert prose with period diction and a grim but fair-minded detective register.

pillars.label: Motive: the dead messenger carried a stolen sample token that could expose a warehouse theft ring
Opportunity: the killer could move between Bluegate Yard, the river stair, and Liddell's warehouse under cover of rain
Connection: the victim's last errand tied him to the warehouse scales, not to a street quarrel
Alibis and contradictions: the poor visible suspect looks guilty, but the timings and corroboration clear him

cast.surface_role: costermonger who found the body and fears the police will blame the nearest poor man

fact.value: knife-grinder and lodging-house tenant; visible suspect who drank with the victim

clues.hook_text: Maud's shawl is still wet from kneeling by the corpse; she keeps glancing toward the lodging-house steps, angry that the constable's first question was whether the drunk knife-grinder had done it.

fact.value: person:arthur_liddell

clues.hook_text: Maud heard the dying man mutter one clipped warehouse name before the rain swallowed it; she is frightened of repeating it because foremen can ruin a street trader with one complaint.

fact.value: Maud saw Jonas Bell stagger from the public-house yard with a dark-stained knife in his hand after drinking with the victim

clues.hook_text: Maud saw a blade in the gaslight and has been clinging to that simple answer, though her voice hardens whenever anyone says hanging a poor drunk is tidy work.

fact.value: Nell Carter was beside Maud at the barrow when the cry over the body went up, shaking so hard she spilled her match tray

clues.hook_text: Maud snaps at anyone who bullies Nell; the girl may have seen something, but Maud insists she was not alone long enough to kill a dock messenger.

cast.surface_role: match-seller who sleeps near the yard and notices movements respectable men ignore

fact.value: the dead man's last errand will lead investigators from the yard to the warehouse scales

clues.hook_text: Nell keeps rubbing blue chalk-dust from under her thumbnail; she heard a gentleman's threat by the warehouse wall but fears a magistrate will believe his collar before her hunger.

fact.value: used the side river gate from place:liddell_warehouse toward place:bluegate_yard shortly before the body was found

clues.hook_text: Nell can tell carts by sound; when pressed past her terror, she describes one quiet tread that should not have been in the yard after the warehouse bell.

fact.value: place:liddell_warehouse

clues.hook_text: Nell points not toward the gin-shop but toward the warehouse lamps, where one upper window kept burning after all honest loading had ceased.

fact.value: Maud Greaves stayed at her barrow arguing with a constable until the alarm, with three customers sheltering under her awning

clues.hook_text: Nell resents Maud's fussing but defends her fiercely; the old costermonger was too loud and too public to slip away into murder.

cast.surface_role: senior St. Bride Inquiry Bureau partner, impatient for proof but not for a convenient hanging

fact.value: the killing was done after a deliberate meeting about warehouse business, not during a drunken street fight

clues.hook_text: Reed crouches in the rain until his knees crack, tracing where the dead man's boots skidded; he distrusts the neat constable's story because the body lies too carefully for a tavern quarrel.

fact.value: the warehouse scales record sample-token weights and would show whether a messenger's token was false

clues.hook_text: Reed keeps tapping his notebook beside the word 'scales,' a professional habit from older dock cases where brass tokens mattered more than blood on cobbles.

fact.value: Edmund Reed reached Bluegate Yard only after the runner summoned St. Bride from the briefing room

clues.hook_text: Reed's coat is dry under the cape where the killer's would be soaked through; he is old enough to be offended by being counted out, but precise enough to log his own arrival.

fact.value: dock warehouse foreman and true culprit behind the murder

clues.hook_text: When the token, the gate, and Bell's broken alibi are laid in order, Reed stops trying to protect the Bureau's pride and says the ugly conclusion aloud.

cast.surface_role: drunken knife-grinder and lodging-house tenant, frightened because the case fits him too easily

fact.value: recover an incriminating stolen sample token before it exposes his profitable theft ring

clues.hook_text: Jonas reeks of gin and shame, but his terror sharpens when Clara mentions a brass token the dead man flashed in the public house and would not let Jonas touch.

fact.value: Jonas Bell was locked inside the lodging-house entry by the landlord's chain before the fatal window, with his sister pounding on the door for him to answer

clues.hook_text: Jonas keeps swearing he cannot remember the walk home, then grows furious at the one humiliating detail that could save him: he was too drunk and too locked-in to reach the yard.

fact.value: intended to take a brass sample token to the warehouse scales before meeting anyone at Bluegate Yard

clues.hook_text: Under bluster, Jonas remembers the victim sobering suddenly over a scrap of paper, as if a poor messenger had found a way to frighten a rich man's warehouse.

fact.value: Jonas thought Nell Carter brushed the victim's coat for coin and may have taken the brass token

clues.hook_text: Jonas points at Nell too quickly, not with cruelty but panic; he saw small fingers near the victim's pocket and wants any story that is not the noose around his own neck.

cast.surface_role: dock warehouse foreman with polished cuffs, wet boots, and too much interest in the dead man's pockets

fact.value: kept the master key to the side river gate connecting place:liddell_warehouse with the passage toward place:bluegate_yard

clues.hook_text: Liddell offers his keys one by one like a man performing honesty, but his thumb never leaves the smallest iron key on the ring.

fact.value: Arthur Liddell claims he was alone at the warehouse ledger desk during the murder window, balancing the scales accounts

clues.hook_text: His ledger is beautifully ruled, every figure clean as church silver; the neatness itself feels like a freshly scrubbed doorstep after blood.

fact.value: recognized the missing sample token before Clara described it, then tried to pretend all such tokens were ordinary

clues.hook_text: The first time Clara says 'brass,' Liddell's hand goes to his waistcoat pocket; only afterward does he remember to smile.

fact.value: Arthur Liddell insists Jonas Bell's trade knife and drunken quarrel make him the only sensible suspect

clues.hook_text: Liddell speaks Jonas's name with practised contempt, as if poverty itself were a signed confession.

goal_statement: Solve the murder of the dock messenger in Bluegate Yard and prove the killer before an innocent man is fitted for the noose.
intro: London, 1888: in the docklands off Ratcliff Highway, Bluegate Yard lies under river fog, gaslight, and rain, and a dock messenger has been found dead on the wet cobbles. You are a newly trusted detective-operative of the small St. Bride Inquiry Bureau, called in plain clothes before the Metropolitan Police can make a tidy case of the nearest poor man with a bad night behind him. In these streets, public-house talk, cab-wheel marks, river mud, and the set of a wound may weigh more than a sworn accusation, because a clean-looking answer can still put an innocent neck in the rope.
premise: In London in 1888, amid the soot, gaslight, river fog, and dock traffic off Ratcliff Highway, a murdered dock messenger is found in Bluegate Yard and the small plain-clothes St. Bride Inquiry Bureau is brought in before the Metropolitan Police can take over. As newly assigned detective-operative Clara Vale, you work the case through body marks, wet cobbles, public houses, river stairs, cabmen, costermongers, and suspect lodgings, in a system where hurried officials and frightened witnesses can turn a poor visible suspect into the easiest man to hang.
